grader.scenario: Static IP block (/29) routing failure on S-Net Business Fibre after an overnight exchange maintenance window
grader.notes: Strong technical diagnostic call where Marcus verifies PIN/address early ([00:24]–[00:32]), shows warm empathy ([00:13], [01:04]), paraphrases accurately ([01:14]), listens closely to complex routing details (AL hard PASS), and remains polite to the customer (R hard PASS). However, at [05:36]–[06:50] he fails Ownership (O hard FAIL) by blaming the internal core network team ('sort their mess out'), and fails Resolution (RE hard FAIL) as the `/29` subnet remains unreachable at call end.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: At [00:13] and [01:04], Marcus expresses clear empathy for the outage impact on Adebayo's freight logistics operation, Dover/Felixstowe depots, and warehouse scanners.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Marcus accurately tracks every technical detail Adebayo shares—including `81.144.210.48/29`, the Meraki MX68, `.49` VPN, `.50` WMS server, `.51` HMRC gateway, `172.16.250.114` anchor IP, and hop 3 at `bng-croydon-02` ([07:14], [11:06]).

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: At [05:36], Marcus says: 'Honestly, Adebayo, that's the core network team's problem—they broke the BGP routing table during last night's maintenance and there's nothing I can do from here, you'll have to wait for them to sort their mess out.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Although Marcus blames the internal network team at [05:36] and [06:50], he remains consistently polite, respectful, and courteous toward Adebayo personally throughout the call ([00:13], [06:01], [07:14], [12:49]).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: At [07:37], Marcus states that `81.144.210.48/29` is still unreachable and will remain offline until Tier 3 applies the BGP fix around 14:00, and at [12:06] Adebayo notes the `/29` block is still offline at call close.
